Weighted 1D histogram

Source: R/kernel-smoothing.R
hist.weighted.Rd

Bins x into breaks and sums weight (instead of counting) within each bin, returning both counts and a weighted density (counts divided by total weight and by bin width) plus bin midpoints — the building block for the non-parametric weekly/monthly/trend estimators.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'weighted'
hist(x, weight, breaks)

# S3 method for class 'weighted.1D'
hist(x, weight, breaks)

Arguments

x

Numeric vector of values to bin.

weight

Numeric vector of weights, same length as x (e.g. the EM background/trigger probabilities).

breaks

Numeric vector of bin edges; must span the range of x (an error otherwise).

Value

A list with breaks, counts (summed weight per bin), density (counts normalised to integrate to 1 over breaks), and mids (bin midpoints).

A note on the name

Despite the dots, this is an ordinary function, not an S3 method for the graphics::hist() generic — the name is inherited from the original D'Angelo et al. (2024) script. It has to be exported with an explicit @rawNamespace directive because roxygen2 otherwise reads hist.weighted as hist dispatching on class "weighted" and registers it as a method, which both hides the function from users and makes hist() misbehave on any object that happens to carry that class.

References

D'Angelo et al. (2024); see spHawkes-package.

Examples

x <- c(0.2, 0.4, 1.3, 2.7, 2.9)
w <- c(1, 2, 1, 1, 3)
h <- hist.weighted(x, w, breaks = 0:3)
h$counts
#> 1 2 3 
#> 3 1 4 
h$density
#>     1     2     3 
#> 0.375 0.125 0.500
